study: Readings named by their time: a running sum that a model can learn to write
kind: pre-registration of a screen on the laptop's GPU: the stack with line heads and the same-size Transformer on a corpus of three families, one seed
why: written_chains_four_families.json: neither model learned the running sum of a row of readings, written as sums or as tots. Over 1 to 4 steps four-stack answers 0.109 and 0.090 of them, the guess floor, in 45 to 60 bytes: it does not find the row even for one reading, though the same model learned hops (0.993) and offs (0.979). In hops and offs every written step goes on from a run of bytes that stands in the line, a name and its '='. In sums and tots a step is found by its place in a row, and the query (+mx=) shares no run of bytes with the row it asks for (mx:774). That record's rule for a family that neither arm learns is to change how its chain is written before it is practised. Telemetry names a reading by its channel and its time, and that is the change: in the family ticks (experiments/task_families.py, 11e0518) every reading is an item of its own, named by its channel's letter and its tick's letter; the ticks of a channel run on through the alphabet from a start drawn evenly, and the item at the tick after a channel's last reading ends it. A written step is the last digit of the sum so far and the name of the next tick, and the step after it looks that name up: one lookup by a name and one addition of two digits, as in offs, with the next name worked out and not looked up. The running sum is the skill the one-model plan needs for telemetry.

family.a line: mk=7;ml=7;mm=4;mn=.;...;@mk=8 and, written, @mk=7ml=4mm=8mn=8: channel m read 7 at tick k, 7 at l and 4 at m, and at n it ends; the sum's last digit is written after every reading with the next tick's name, and once more as the answer where the channel ends.
family.items: 24 a line in random order, readings and channel ends together; beside the query's channel, channels of one to four readings; a channel's letter stands for one channel in a line, and channels share ticks.
family.steps: The readings of the query's channel. A chain of n steps takes 4n + 2 bytes, 50 at 12 steps.

guess floors (4,000 lines a cell, seed 3.2 to 12 steps: 0.097 to 0.108 for every guess: the answer is even over the digits

corpus.file: data/onemodel/chains/ticks-1-4-written.bin, written by experiments/task_families.py corpus --families hops offs ticks --steps 1 2 3 4 --seed 1 --written-chains with the frozen code copy 11e0518
corpus.note: hops and offs draw their lines as in the four-family corpus (the generator's lines of the four older families are the same bytes at 11e0518 as at 833ff4d). sums and tots are left out.

arms.tick-stack: the laptop's delayed test bed with line heads, four-line-stack's recipe of line_heads_four_families.json (5,252,132 parameters), from scratch, trained on streams of 10 windows
arms.tick-tf-chain: the test bed's Transformer (--variant transformer --dim 256 --depth 6 --heads 4 --mlp-ratio 4; 4,792,320 parameters) from chain-tf's averaged weights (--initialize-from, sha256 32fc2e8a...), the Transformer's base by the rule of four_families_transformer_again.json: it follows names when it starts

training: Each arm 24,000 updates with only the corpus changed from its earlier run: experiments/train_event_lm.py --corpus data/onemodel/chains/ticks-1-4-written.bin --ctx 256 --bs 16 --steps 24000 --warmup 300 --lr 1.2e-3 --wd 0.05 --seed 20001 --rotated-adam 50 --weight-average 0.999, the stack with the bed's switches, --read-by-cell and --read-word-heads 2 --read-word-unit line --read-word-span 256. Frozen code copy 11e0518, whose trainer and model are 833ff4d's; only the family was added. On the laptop's GPU, one run at a time after four-cell-stack of line_heads_four_families.json has trained: tick-stack, then tick-tf-chain, then tick-tf. The laptop has no CUDA device, so the trainer's fast paths do not apply, and line heads take no fused reads on any device; both of the server's GPUs carry full-size runs that train alone until Sunday.
measure: With each arm's averaged weights, experiments/practice_loop.py --families hops offs ticks --evaluate 1 2 3 4 5 6 8 12 --evaluate-tasks 200 --max-bytes 64 --seed 0 on the laptop with the frozen copy 11e0518: for every family and step count the accuracy of the last byte, the share of answers that write the whole chain as the corpus writes it, each with its 95% Wilson interval, and the mean bytes written.

reading.(1) learned: An arm has learned a family if its mean accuracy over 1 to 4 steps is at least 0.95 and its mean share of whole chains over 1 to 4 steps at least 0.90, the mark of written_chains_four_families.json. Read for each of the nine pairs of arm and family.
reading.(2) the running sum: Written with its times the running sum is learnable if tick-stack has learned ticks by (1).
reading.(3) sharing: The third family costs the lookups nothing if tick-stack has learned hops and offs by (1); four-line-stack's accuracies on the two, read for line_heads_four_families.json, are reported beside.
reading.(4) reach without practice: For every learned pair: its chains reach past the trained length if at 8 steps the accuracy is at least 0.50 with at least half of the answers writing the whole chain; reported at 5, 6 and 12 steps as well.
reading.(5) the stack against the Transformer: Reported for every family at every step count; a family that one model learns and the other does not is stated, with the starts said: tick-stack and tick-tf start from nothing, tick-tf-chain from weights that follow names.
reading.scope: One seed and synthetic lines: a screen of which chains a small model learns to write, not a claim about reasoning in language or about telemetry.

what follows: If tick-stack has learned all three families, they go into the practice loop together (rehearsal, the cap at 12, the loop of line_heads_four_families.json) as the next registration on the server's GPU, with the Transformer arm that learned the most families as its control, and the one-model plan writes telemetry's readings with their times. If it has not learned ticks, what it writes at 1 and 2 steps is read first, and the step's writing is changed next (the reading written beside the sum), recorded as that. If it has lost hops or offs, the shares of the families in the corpus are the next question.
seen_before_recording: written_chains_four_families.json's and four_families_transformer_again.json's results; line_heads.json's and line_heads_in_practice.json's results; the new family's lines, tests and guess floors; four-line-stack's training log (trained 11:45 UTC today, not yet evaluated by family) and a check of the evaluator with its weights on six tasks a cell at 1 and 2 steps of the three families (hops and offs all right; ticks, which it never saw, all wrong in 11 bytes). No model has been trained on a corpus that holds ticks.
